quickAnswer.question: How much does a Singapore-Malaysia package cost from Trivandrum?
quickAnswer.answer: iWay Tourism's Singapore-Malaysia combo packages from Trivandrum Airport start at ₹45,000 per person for a budget 4N/5D express trip covering core city highlights. The standard 7N/8D package ranges from ₹75,000–₹95,000 including Genting Highlands and Sentosa Island. Premium 9N/10D packages with luxury cruises and 4-star hotels range from ₹1,00,000–₹1,34,000+. All packages include return flights, visa, hotels, transfers, and sightseeing.

overview: Singapore and Malaysia remain the most requested international combo package from South India for good reason — they are geographically adjacent, logistically seamless, and offer contrasting experiences that complement each other perfectly. Singapore delivers futuristic urban design, world-class theme parks, and immaculate public infrastructure. Malaysia offers cultural depth through the Batu Caves and Kuala Lumpur's Malay-Chinese-Indian heritage, the cool highland air of Genting and Cameron Highlands, and a food culture that South Indian travellers immediately connect with.

What makes iWay Tourism's Singapore-Malaysia packages different from the aggregator templates is the routing. We fly you from Trivandrum (TRV) — no connecting flight through Delhi or Mumbai. We handle the Singapore and Malaysia visas as a combined submission. We design the itinerary so the border crossing between Singapore and Malaysia (via the Johor Bahru causeway or a domestic flight) happens at the midpoint of the trip, not as a rushed last-day transfer. And every group gets a dedicated coordinator reachable by WhatsApp throughout the trip.

itineraryHighlights.title: Singapore City & Gardens by the Bay
itineraryHighlights.description: Arrive at Changi Airport. Explore the Marina Bay Sands observation deck, the Supertree Grove light show at Gardens by the Bay, and the cultural quarters of Chinatown and Little India. Evening at Clarke Quay riverside.

itineraryHighlights.title: Sentosa Island
itineraryHighlights.description: Full day at Sentosa — Universal Studios Singapore, the S.E.A. Aquarium, cable car ride, and Palawan Beach. Evening at Resorts World for dining.

itineraryHighlights.title: Singapore Night Safari & Transfer to Malaysia
itineraryHighlights.description: Morning free for Orchard Road shopping. Afternoon Night Safari — the world's first nocturnal wildlife park. Evening transfer to Malaysia via the Johor Bahru causeway or domestic flight to Kuala Lumpur.

itineraryHighlights.title: Kuala Lumpur & Batu Caves
itineraryHighlights.description: Petronas Twin Towers (view deck or KLCC Park), the colourful 272-step staircase of Batu Caves, Central Market for handicrafts, and Jalan Alor for Malaysia's legendary street food scene.

itineraryHighlights.title: Genting Highlands
itineraryHighlights.description: Cable car ascent to Genting Highlands at 1,800 metres — cool mountain air, Skytropolis indoor theme park, and the casino complex (for adults). Return to KL for evening departure or continue to cruise embarkation.

visaInfo.heading: Singapore & Malaysia Visa for Indian Passport Holders

quickAnswer.question: Do Indians need a visa for Singapore and Malaysia?
quickAnswer.answer: Yes, Indian passport holders require a visa for both Singapore and Malaysia. Singapore uses an electronic visa (e-visa) system that iWay processes in 3–5 working days. Malaysia requires a separate eNTRI or eVISA depending on the travel purpose, processed in 2–4 working days. Both visa applications are included in every iWay Tourism package — we handle the forms, document preparation, and submission.

body: Singapore e-visa requirements: valid passport (minimum 6 months validity), completed application form, recent passport-size photograph, confirmed return flight booking, and proof of hotel reservation. Processing time: 3–5 working days. Cost: included in the package.

Malaysia eNTRI/eVISA requirements: valid passport, application form, photograph, flight booking, and hotel confirmation. Processing time: 2–4 working days. The eNTRI is simpler and suitable for tourism stays under 15 days. Cost: included in the package.

iWay Tourism submits both visa applications simultaneously after receiving your passport copies and photographs. We track the status and notify you of approval. In the rare event of a rejection, we guide you through the reapplication process.

bestTimeToVisit.heading: Best Time to Visit Singapore & Malaysia

quickAnswer.question: When is the best time to visit Singapore and Malaysia from India?
quickAnswer.answer: Singapore is a year-round destination with consistent tropical weather (27–32°C). Malaysia's west coast (Kuala Lumpur, Genting) is best from May to September, while the east coast peaks from March to October. For the combined trip, May to September offers the most reliable weather across both countries. Avoid the Indian school holiday rush (May–June) if you prefer smaller crowds and better hotel rates.

bestTimeToVisit.body: Singapore has no distinct seasons — it's tropical year-round with afternoon rain showers that pass quickly. Malaysia's weather varies by coast: the west coast (where KL and Genting are located) receives less rain from May to September, while the east coast monsoon hits November to February. For the combined Singapore-Malaysia trip, the sweet spot is March to May or September to November — good weather in both countries and lower crowd density than the Indian summer holiday peak.

faqs.question: Can I do Singapore only or Malaysia only instead of the combo?
faqs.answer: Yes. We offer standalone Singapore packages (3N/4D to 5N/6D) and standalone Malaysia packages (4N/5D to 7N/8D). However, the combo is our most popular option because the two countries are geographically adjacent — the border crossing adds only 1–2 hours — and combining them delivers far more variety per rupee spent.

faqs.question: Is the Genting Dream Cruise worth adding to the package?
faqs.answer: If your budget allows, the 2N/3D cruise is one of the most valued upgrades our clients report. The cruise departs from Singapore and covers the open sea with ports of call that vary by sailing. All meals are included on board, entertainment is extensive, and the experience of waking up on the ocean is a highlight that land-based itineraries cannot replicate. The upgrade adds approximately ₹20,000–₹35,000 per person depending on cabin class.

faqs.question: How much spending money should I carry for a 7-day Singapore-Malaysia trip?
faqs.answer: For a standard package where meals beyond breakfast, shopping, and personal expenses are not included, we recommend carrying approximately ₹25,000–₹40,000 per person (or the equivalent in SGD/MYR). Singapore is noticeably more expensive than Malaysia for food and shopping. Hawker centres in Singapore offer excellent meals for SGD 4–8 (₹250–500). Malaysian street food is even more affordable at MYR 5–15 (₹90–275) per meal.
